subject.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]

question: Should accessor-method names be rejected only as ordinary merge-patch object fields, or become globally invalid identifiers across every schema-declared config record map?
rationale: The PR’s security hardening changes an existing compatibility boundary: global rejection is stricter but can silently drop previously valid record IDs, while schema-aware rejection preserves configuration semantics and requires a more precise implementation.

options.title: Preserve record-map IDs
options.body: Reject the four names as ordinary object fields while allowing them at schema-declared record/map ID positions, with regression tests for representative maps.

options.title: Ban the identifiers globally
options.body: Make the names invalid across config schemas, add explicit validation and doctor migration behavior, and prove upgrades fail clearly rather than silently dropping values.

recommendation.title: Preserve record-map IDs
recommendation.body: Reject the four names as ordinary object fields while allowing them at schema-declared record/map ID positions, with regression tests for representative maps.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Control UI security and assistant-media history makes steipete the strongest available owner for the cross-cutting gateway/config boundary decision.
